mainTopic: Meat and milk absorbed into each other: רב's pot of milk, lashes for half-and-half eating and cooking, and the dispute over אפשר לסוחטו.
overview: Earlier, רב ruled that when a כזית of meat falls into a pot of milk, the meat becomes forbidden but the milk stays permitted. The גמרא asks why, since the milk that soaked into the meat should be forbidden. A first answer says the Torah forbids only the meat (the גדי), not the milk. That answer falls, because רב also gives lashes for eating half a כזית of meat cooked with half a כזית of milk, so he must count the milk as forbidden too. The final answer: the meat fell into a boiling pot, where it soaks milk in but does not let it out, and it was taken out before the pot cooled. The גמרא then examines that half-and-half ruling itself. רב says the halves do not join, and the lashes for eating apply only to food from a large pot. לוי disagrees and gives lashes for cooking too. Last, the גמרא shows that אפשר לסוחטו (absorbed taste that could be squeezed out) is argued about by רבי יהודה and חכמים. רבי's compromise, about whether the pot was stirred and covered, shows that he holds such a piece stays forbidden.

steps.title: Why is the milk permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling that the pot of milk stays permitted, because the milk absorbed into the meat should count as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is the milk permitted? That absorbed milk is forbidden milk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's case of meat that fell into milk and asks why he lets the milk in the pot be used. The milk that soaked into the meat should have become forbidden itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some milk soaked into the meat and became forbidden, like a נבלה. When it seeps back into the pot, it should forbid the whole pot. That clashes with רב's ruling that the milk is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (asking for the reason behind a ruling)
Permitted
Literally 'נבלה milk': milk that has itself become a forbidden item

phrases.english: Why is the milk permitted?
It is forbidden milk!

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלָב אַמַּאי מוּתָּר? חָלָב נְבֵלָה הוּא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the meat in רב's earlier ruling to the milk in the same ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the pot of milk stays permitted after a כזית of meat falls in.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The milk absorbed into the meat is itself forbidden. When it comes back out, it should forbid the whole pot.

steps.title: The Torah forbade only the kid, not the milk
steps.stepSummary: רב does hold that absorbed forbidden material counts as forbidden, but meat and milk are different: the פסוק forbids only the meat, not the milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רב holds that what can be squeezed out is forbidden. But here it is different, because the פסוק says 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk': the Torah forbade the kid, not the milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב does hold that absorbed forbidden material counts. But meat and milk is a special case, because the Torah only forbids the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays in place: absorbed forbidden material that could be squeezed out counts as forbidden. The answer makes an exception for בשר בחלב. The פסוק names only the גדי as forbidden, so the milk inside the meat never became forbidden, and the pot stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (the גמרא keeps its earlier position)
What could be squeezed out counts as forbidden: absorbed forbidden material is treated as a forbidden item
There it is different
A young goat; here it stands for the meat

phrases.english: Really, Rav holds
that what can be squeezed out is forbidden,
but there it is different,
because the verse says
'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk' –
the Torah forbade the kid, and not the milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר, וְשָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception from a פסוק: meat and milk differs from the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The milk inside the meat became forbidden, so it should forbid the pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the meat (גדי) is forbidden by the Torah, so the absorbed milk is not forbidden and the pot is permitted.

steps.title: רב lashes for eating half meat and half milk
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person is lashed for eating half a כזית of meat cooked with half a כזית of milk. That only works if the milk counts as forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold that the Torah forbade only the kid and not the milk? But it was stated: if half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of milk were cooked together, רב said he is lashed for eating it but not for cooking it. If the Torah forbade only the kid, why is he lashed for eating? It is only half the minimum amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer using a different ruling of רב. In that ruling, the milk must count toward the forbidden amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes for eating need a full כזית of forbidden food. If only the meat were forbidden, the eater would have had only half a כזית, which is a חצי שיעור, and he would not be lashed. Since רב does give lashes, he must count the milk as forbidden too, which contradicts step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive's volume
Receives lashes (מלקות) from the Torah
Cooking, a separate prohibition of meat and milk
If you were to think...
Less than the minimum amount needed for punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts of רב's ruling. He IS lashed for eating, because together the meat and milk make a full כזית. He is NOT lashed for cooking, because neither item was a full כזית. The challenge comes only from the eating part.

phrases.english: And does Rav hold
that the Torah forbade the kid and not the milk?
But it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חָלָב
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk
that one cooked together,
Rav said: he is lashed for eating it,
but he is not lashed for cooking it.
And if it entered your mind
that the Torah forbade the kid and not the milk,
why is he lashed for eating?
It is only half the required amount!
phrases.notes: Only the half כזית of meat would count, and that is too little for lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב גְּדִי אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה וְלֹא חָלָב? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 using another ruling of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that רב holds only the meat, not the milk, is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב gives lashes for eating a half-and-half כזית. That is only possible if the milk counts as forbidden, so רב must hold the milk is forbidden too.

steps.title: Meat in a boiling pot absorbs but does not release
steps.stepSummary: רב does hold that the milk is forbidden. The pot stays permitted because the meat fell into boiling milk, which it absorbs but does not let back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב really holds that the milk is also forbidden. What case are we dealing with here? Where the meat fell into a boiling pot: it absorbs, but it does not release.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the step 2 answer and gives a new one. It explains רב's original case as a very specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב agrees the absorbed milk is forbidden. In a boiling pot, though, the meat only draws milk in and never pushes it back out. So the forbidden milk stays locked inside the meat and never mixes with the rest of the pot, which stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a ruling to a specific situation)
A boiling pot
It absorbs
It does not release

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds the milk cooked with meat IS forbidden. In his case the milk stays permitted because the meat fell into a boiling pot, where it soaks milk in but does not let it back out. Step 6 completes this answer: the meat was taken out before the pot cooled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much depends on the exact cooking conditions. Whether a food absorbs or releases decides whether the rest of the pot becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav really holds
that the milk is also forbidden,
and here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where it fell into a boiling pot,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כזית of meat from רב's original case.

phrases.english: so that it absorbs,
but does not release.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַב חָלָב נָמֵי אָסוּר, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 3, drops step 2, and answers step 1 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) to a boiling pot.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The milk is not forbidden at all, because the Torah forbade only the גדי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The milk is forbidden, but in a boiling pot the meat does not release it, so the rest of the pot stays permitted.

steps.title: But won't the meat let the milk out when the pot cools?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 4: even if boiling milk only goes into the meat, once the pot cools the meat will release the forbidden milk back into the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when the pot cools down, the meat will release what it absorbed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Boiling may keep the milk inside the meat, but what happens when the pot cools off?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the meat absorbs from the boiling milk but does not release anything. The גמרא points out that this only holds while the pot is boiling. Once it cools, the meat should let the forbidden milk back out, and then the pot of milk should become forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end; ultimately
Cools down; calms (stops boiling)
Releases; lets out what was absorbed

phrases.english: In the end, when it cools down,
phrases.notes: It means the pot. Once it stops boiling, the meat no longer just soaks things in.

phrases.english: it then releases [what it absorbed]!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף כִּי נָיַיח, הֲדַר פָּלֵיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 4 by pointing to what happens after the boiling stops.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that meat falling into boiling milk absorbs but does not release.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not releasing only lasts while the pot is boiling. When it cools, the meat releases the forbidden milk, so the pot should become forbidden.

steps.title: The meat was taken out before the pot cooled
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the person removed the meat quickly, before the pot cooled and before the meat could release anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he removed the meat first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the meat was pulled out of the pot while it was still boiling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the meat would release the milk once the pot cooled. If the meat was taken out before then, it never had the chance to release anything into the pot. So the pot of milk stays permitted, just as רב ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: Did it first; acted early
Removed it

steps.whatToRemember: רב's pot stays permitted because the meat fell into boiling milk, which only goes in, and the meat was removed before the pot cooled.

phrases.english: When he first removed it.
phrases.notes: He took the meat out while the pot was still boiling, before it could cool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation (the meat was removed in time).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat stayed in the pot until it cooled and released the milk.
steps.terutzMaskana: The meat was taken out while the pot was still boiling, so nothing came back out.

steps.title: רב: מלקות for eating half and half, but not for cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רב's ruling quoted earlier: if half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of milk were cooked together, one gets מלקות for eating it, but not for cooking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself: Half an olive-size of meat and half an olive-size of milk that were cooked together. רב said: One is lashed for eating it, but not lashed for cooking it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב's ruling from Step 3 to look at it on its own terms. It is setting up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier this ruling was only used as proof that milk counts as forbidden. Now the גמרא looks at the ruling itself. It notices a split: רב gives מלקות for eating but not for cooking the same mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Now to the matter itself (going back to a statement quoted earlier)
An olive-size, the minimum amount for punishment
Receives מלקות (lashes)
Cooking

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא: חֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וַחֲצִי זַיִת חָלָב
phrases.english: The matter itself: half an olive-size of meat and half an olive-size of milk
phrases.notes: This is רב's ruling that was quoted back in Step 3. Now the גמרא looks at it directly.

phrases.english: that he cooked together with each other,
Rav said: He is lashed for eating it,
but he is not lashed for cooking it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the pot discussion and opens a new look at רב's ruling, which was quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a כזית of meat cooked with half a כזית of milk: מלקות for eating, no מלקות for cooking.

steps.title: Either way, eating and cooking should match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב: if the two halves join to make a full amount, he should get מלקות for cooking too. If they do not join, he should not get מלקות for eating either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: If they join together, he should be lashed for cooking too. If they don't join together, he should not be lashed for eating either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a 'whichever way you look at it' argument. Eating and cooking should get the same treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only question is whether the two halves add up to one full כזית. That answer should be the same for eating and for cooking. רב's split ruling seems to say 'yes' for eating and 'no' for cooking, which does not make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (an either-way argument)
They join together to make up the full amount

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it?
If they join together, he should be lashed for cooking too,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לֹא מִצְטָרְפִין – אַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי לָא לִילְקֵי.
phrases.english: if they don't join together, he should not be lashed for eating either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just presented in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that eating gets מלקות but cooking does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining the two halves is one question with one answer. So eating and cooking should be either both punished or both not punished.

steps.title: They don't join; the eating case is food from a large pot
steps.stepSummary: The halves really do not join. רב's eating case is food taken from a large pot where a lot of meat and milk were cooked together, so it is already one big forbidden mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they do not join together. And the eating case is where the food comes from a large pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that half and half do not join. The eating case is a special one: food taken from a big pot of meat and milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a large amount of meat and milk was cooked together, the whole pot is already one forbidden mixture of בשר בחלב. A כזית taken from it counts in full for eating, even if it is half meat and half milk. But cooking just a half and a half on their own does not make a full amount, so there are no מלקות for cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeping the original position)
A large pot

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב changed his mind about joining. He still holds the halves do not join on their own. The eating case works only because the food comes from a big pot that is already forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, half and half do not join. One gets מלקות for eating only because the food came from a large pot of meat and milk.

phrases.english: Really, they do not join together,
and [the eating case is] where it comes from a large pot.
phrases.notes: A big pot where lots of meat and milk were cooked together, so it's all already forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the either-way challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the either-way argument (they do not join) and explains the eating case as a special situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's two rulings are about the same small mixture, which makes them contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The halves do not join. The eating case is food from a large pot that was already a forbidden mixture.

steps.title: לוי: מלקות for cooking as well
steps.stepSummary: לוי disagrees with רב and holds that one also gets מלקות for cooking half a כזית of meat with half a כזית of milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: He is also lashed for cooking it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion comes in. לוי says one gets מלקות for cooking too, not just for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said no מלקות for cooking. לוי holds that the two halves do join, so cooking them together is also punishable. This sets up a clear disagreement between רב and לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Also; even

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אַף לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ,
phrases.english: And Levi said: He is also lashed for cooking it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אַף לוֹקֶה עַל בִּשּׁוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's ruling from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a כזית of meat cooked with half a כזית of milk: מלקות for cooking as well as for eating.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא: cooking is like eating, if it is real cooking
steps.stepSummary: לוי backs up his view with a ברייתא he taught: just as one gets מלקות for eating, one gets מלקות for cooking. This applies to cooking that makes the food fit for people to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so לוי taught in his collection of teachings: Just as he is lashed for eating it, so too he is lashed for cooking it. And what kind of cooking did they mean? Cooking that makes the food something others would eat because it is cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי brings a ברייתא from his own collection that supports his view. It also defines what counts as 'cooking'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats cooking just like eating, which matches לוי's ruling. It adds a limit: only cooking that makes the food fit to eat counts. Light warming that leaves the food unfit for eating would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: לוי's own collection of ברייתות, not our משנה
Just as
Because of

steps.whatToRemember: רב: מלקות only for eating, and only from a large pot. לוי: מלקות for cooking too, as long as the cooking makes the food fit to eat.

phrases.english: And so Levi taught in his collection of teachings:
Just as he is lashed for eating it,
so too he is lashed for cooking it,
and about which kind of cooking did they say this?
Cooking that others would eat it
phrases.notes: He means it was cooked enough that people would actually eat it.

phrases.english: because of its cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports לוי's ruling from Step 10 with a ברייתא he taught.
steps.raayaObject: לוי's view that one gets מלקות for cooking as well as eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from לוי's collection: cooking is punished like eating, when the cooking makes the food fit to eat.

steps.title: Squeezable taste is a dispute among the תנאים: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question of אפשר לסוחטו is a מחלוקת תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה holds that a piece flavored by a drop of milk becomes forbidden itself and then forbids all the other pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where the forbidden taste can be squeezed out is itself argued about by the תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if a drop of milk fell on a piece of meat and gave it taste, that piece itself becomes forbidden like נבלה. It then forbids all the other pieces, because they are the same kind of food. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier question: is a piece forbidden even if the absorbed taste could be squeezed out? It shows that this exact point is argued about in a ברייתא, and it starts with רבי יהודה's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that once the milk flavors the piece, the whole piece becomes a forbidden item in its own right, even though the milk could in theory be squeezed out. Because that piece is now fully forbidden meat, it is mixed with other meat of its own kind. So it is not cancelled out (בטל) and it forbids every piece in the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to squeeze it out: the forbidden taste could in theory be pressed out of the piece
It is a dispute among the תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)
Gave taste: the milk's flavor entered the meat
The piece becomes like נבלה, meaning it is treated as a forbidden item in its own right
Its own kind: same-type food that does not cancel it out

steps.confusionAlert: נבלה here does not mean the animal died without proper שחיטה. It means the piece now counts as fully forbidden food in its own right.

phrases.english: And the case where it is possible to squeeze it out, itself
phrases.notes: This goes back to an earlier question on the daf: is a piece forbidden if the absorbed taste could be squeezed out?

phrases.english: is a dispute among the Tannaim,
as it is taught in a baraita:
A drop of milk that fell on the piece of meat,
once it gave taste into the piece,
the piece itself becomes like a forbidden carcass,
and it forbids all the pieces, every one of them,
because they are its own kind;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ עַצְמוֹ תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב and לוי discussion about cooking and goes back to the earlier question of אפשר לסוחטו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a piece flavored by milk becomes forbidden in its own right, even though the milk could be squeezed out. It then forbids all the same-kind pieces in the pot.

steps.title: חכמים: forbidden only if the milk flavors the whole pot
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה. Nothing is forbidden unless the drop of milk is strong enough to give taste to the gravy, the spices and all the pieces together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: it is not forbidden unless the milk gives taste to the gravy, the spices and the pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side of the argument, the view of חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים do not treat the first piece as becoming forbidden on its own. They look at the whole pot. The milk spreads through everything, so we measure it against all the contents together. Only if it can flavor all of that is anything forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Gravy or broth in the pot
Spices or seasonings in the pot
Not until it gives taste: the minimum needed to make it forbidden

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
not unless it gives taste into the gravy
and into the spices and into the pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nothing is forbidden unless the milk gives taste to the entire contents of the pot.

steps.title: רבי's compromise: it depends on stirring and covering
steps.stepSummary: רבי says each view fits a different case. רבי יהודה is right when the pot was not stirred and not covered. חכמים are right when it was stirred and covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה's view seems right when the person did not stir and did not cover the pot. The view of חכמים seems right when he stirred and covered it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) steps in and divides the two opinions into two different cooking situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring and covering spread the milk evenly through the whole pot. In that case it makes sense to measure the milk against everything, as חכמים say. Without them, the milk first goes into the one piece and makes it forbidden in its own right. That piece then forbids all the other pieces, as רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: His words seem right: a way of agreeing with an opinion in a certain case
Stirred the pot
Covered the pot

steps.whyThisMatters: This compromise shapes how later halacha thinks about a drop falling into a pot: whether it was stirred and covered matters.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem correct
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: when he did not stir and did not cover,
and the words of the Sages when he stirred and covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the רבי יהודה and חכמים dispute by giving each view its own case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the pot was not stirred or covered, רבי יהודה's view applies. If it was stirred and covered, the view of חכמים applies.

steps.title: What does 'not stirred and not covered' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact case רבי meant by 'did not stir and did not cover'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he did not stir and did not cover' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of רבי's words. This sets up the next move, where it will test possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's line could mean several things, such as never stirring at all or stirring only at certain times. The גמרא needs to pin this down, because only a precise case will make רבי יהודה's ruling make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of: asks for a definition

phrases.english: What is meant by "he did not stir and did not cover"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clear definition of the case in רבי's compromise.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact circumstances of 'not stirred and not covered' in which רבי יהודה's view applies.

steps.title: It cannot mean never stirred or covered at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the simplest reading, that the pot was never stirred or covered at all, and rejects it. In that case the piece takes in the milk but never gives it out, so it could not forbid the other pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he did not stir at all and did not cover at all, that cannot be right. The piece only absorbs the milk; it does not release it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a first meaning for רבי's words and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the flavored piece forbids all the other pieces. For that to happen, the piece must release its forbidden taste into the pot. If there was no stirring or covering at all, the piece only soaks up the milk and gives nothing back. So there is no way for the other pieces to become forbidden, and this reading cannot be what רבי meant.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggested reading that is about to be rejected
At all
It certainly absorbs
It does not release or give out

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not with the first piece becoming forbidden; it absorbed the milk. The problem is רבי יהודה's claim that it forbids the OTHER pieces, which needs the taste to come back out.

phrases.english: If you say he did not stir at all,
and did not cover at all,
it does absorb,
but it does not release.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the point unsaid: so how could this piece forbid the other pieces?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לֹא נִיעֵר כְּלָל, וְלֹא כִּסָּה כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 15 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'not stirred and not covered' as meaning no stirring or covering at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With no stirring or covering at all, the flavored piece only absorbs and never releases. So it could not forbid the other pieces, as רבי יהודה claims.

steps.title: Second reading: stirred and covered only at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to read רבי's case as a pot that was stirred and covered only later. Then it asks why everything is forbidden, since the piece gives the milk back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he did not stir at the beginning, only at the end, and did not cover at the beginning, only at the end. But then why is everything forbidden? The milk that the piece took in, it also gives back out!
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first reading in step 16, the גמרא offers a new one: the pot was not stirred or covered right away, only later. It immediately challenges this reading too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the piece takes in the milk first. Later the stirring and covering spread the milk through the whole pot. So the milk ends up mixed into everything and should be nullified by the large amount, just as חכמים say. Why, then, does רבי say רבי יהודה is right and all the pieces are forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: stirred (the pot)
covered (the pot)
at the beginning / at the end
absorbed, took in
expelled, gave back out

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is that nothing at all was absorbed. The piece did absorb the milk. The question is that it later released that same milk into the whole pot, where it should be nullified.

phrases.english: Rather, he did not stir at the beginning
but only at the end,
and he did not cover at the beginning
but only at the end,
Why (is everything forbidden)? What it absorbed, it also gives out!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, לֹא נִיעֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of רבי's case after step 16 rejected the first, and then challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי's case means stirring and covering only at the end
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the piece later releases the milk into the whole pot, the milk should be nullified there, so the pieces should not all be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי holds that something that can be squeezed out is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור. The piece became forbidden when it absorbed the milk, even though the milk later comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that something that can be squeezed out is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 17. רבי holds that once a piece took in forbidden taste, it stays forbidden, even though that taste could be squeezed out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The piece took in the milk at the start and became forbidden itself. Later the milk comes out, but the piece does not become permitted again, because רבי holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור. So this second reading works, and it shows that the question of step 12 is really what this ברייתא is arguing about.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (this view)
something whose forbidden taste can be squeezed out is still forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's case of 'did not stir and did not cover' means stirring and covering only at the end. רבי still forbids everything there because he holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof from step 12 that אפשר לסוחטו is a מחלוקת תנאים. It shows this ברייתא really does take a position on that question.

phrases.english: He holds that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by explaining which view רבי holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the view that the speaker holds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the piece later gives the milk back out, it should not stay forbidden, and the milk should be nullified in the pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור, so the piece became forbidden when it absorbed the milk and stays forbidden.
